 Late Malaysian billionaire Lim Goh Tong's grandson loses bid to remove administrators in Genting family will dispute
 By Hien Nguyen    November 15, 2026 | 03:10 pm PT 
 Get VnExpress first in Google Search 
 See more of the news you trust. Make VnExpress a preferred source to prioritise our updates in your Google search results
 Marcus Chan, a grandson of late Malaysian billionaire Lim Goh Tong, has failed in his attempt to remove the court-appointed administrators managing his late mother’s disputed RM1.6 billion (US$400 million) estate. 
 High Court judge Mahazan Mat Taib last Friday rejected Marcus' application as he had not provided sufficient grounds for the removal of the two court-appointed administrators overseeing his mother Lim Siew Kim's disputed estate.
 The court also lifted an interim injunction previously obtained by Marcus that had barred the administrators from acting for the estate, allowing them to resume their duties.
 It further ordered RM30,000 in costs to be paid to the administrators, The Edge Malaysia reported.
 Marcus, Siew Kim's only son and a 30% beneficiary of her residuary estate, had applied to have the administrators removed over allegations including unauthorized payments for legal services, improper handling of estate assets, interference in companies associated with his mother and conflicts of interest.
 Marcus Chan Jau Chwen, son of the late Lim Siew Kim. Photo from Anglo-Eastern Plantations' website
 His lawyer previously claimed that the administrators had paid their legal fees from the estate without obtaining approval, despite an earlier order requiring payments relating to debts other than Siew Kim's to be subject to the court's scrutiny.
 Mahazan said on Friday that the phrasing of the appointment order showed that the administrators were responsible for exercising their own independent professional judgment in managing and preserving the estate.
 It did not expressly require them to seek judicial approval for every payment or administrative decision or before exercising every power already conferred upon them, she said.
 Regarding the other allegations, Mahazan found that there was insufficient evidence of unlawful corporate intervention or misuse of estate funds serious enough to warrant the administrators' removal.
 "However, the dismissal of (Marcus') application does not amount to blanket approval of every expenditure or transaction undertaken by the administrators," she said, as quoted by the New Straits Times .
 "Their obligations to account for estate assets, comply with the appointment order and submit their costs and remuneration for examination remain unaffected."
 Marcus has indicated that he would appeal Friday's ruling.
 The administrators were appointed by the court in November 2023 to manage the estate pending a larger ongoing court case over the inheritance, which Marcus' application is a part of.
 Chan T'Shiao Li and Kimberly Chan T'Shiao Miin, two of Siew Kim's daughters, had filed the suit to challenge the validity of their mother's will , which left them only fractions of the estate while their brother Marcus and another sister were given company shares, safe deposit boxes and properties.
 Siew Kim, who died from cancer in July 2022 at the age of 73, was the third child and youngest daughter of Goh Tong, founder of the Genting business empire and Malaysia's third-richest man when he died in October 2007, according to Forbes.
 The plaintiffs pointed to two earlier wills drawn up within months of the final version that set out markedly different distributions of the estate, arguing that the final will did not reflect their mother's true intentions or her sound judgment at the time.
 Marcus is one of the defendants in the case. The others include the lawyer who drafted the final will and the estate’s executors and trustees, Malcolm Fernandez and Chan Mei Yee.
 The trial for the will dispute is scheduled to continue in January next year.
